title: Section 80D Health Insurance Deduction
source: Income Tax Department, Government of India (Income Tax Act 1961 & Income Tax Act 2025)
reference: Section 80D, Income Tax Act 1961 — recodified as Section 126 under Income Tax Act 2025
content: Section 80D (recodified as Section 126 under the Income Tax Act 2025) provides tax deduction on medical insurance premiums paid for self, family (spouse and dependent children), and parents. For individuals under 60 years of age, the maximum deduction limit for self and family is ₹25,000 per financial year. An additional deduction of ₹25,000 is available for health insurance premiums paid for parents under 60 years. If parents are senior citizens (aged 60 years or above), the deduction limit increases to ₹50,000 per financial year. If both the taxpayer and parents are senior citizens, the maximum combined deduction limit under Section 80D (Section 126) is ₹1,00,000 (₹50,000 + ₹50,000). Preventive health checkups up to ₹5,000 within the overall cap are also eligible under Section 80D (Section 126). This deduction is allowed only under the Old Tax Regime.
